exposure: Late preterm ECV (36-37 weeks) vs. Term ECV (>37 weeks)
Timing of external cephalic version (ECV) (late preterm vs. term)
cohort: Pregnant women who underwent external cephalic version (ECV) for non-cephalic presentation (n=597)
finding: While the success rate of ECV was similar between late preterm and term groups, initiating ECV before term was associated with increased rates of preterm delivery, early term delivery, and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Timing of ECV did not significantly affect the rates of vaginal delivery or intrapartum cesarean delivery.
